the rate of ATRP from a surface is enhanced as the initiator graft density is increased.
the rate of polymerization in surface-initiated atom-transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP) is enhanced by the presence of a large number of initiator groups on the surface of a substrate.
the kinetics of surface-initiated ATrp is strongly influenced by graft density.

the development of new materials for use in nanotechnology and biomedicine.
the design of molecular architectures for the development of advanced materials.
the design of molecular architectures from surfaces by the surface-initiated polymerization of styrene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of ATRP is increased by a factor of seven for the most densely functionalized surface, and the kinetics can be described by the same phenomenological kinetic model as bulk kinetics.

surface-initiated ATEP of styrene from functionalized montmorilonite clay is a viable method for the synthesis of well-defined polystyrene-grafted clay nanocomposite materials, and that graft density has a profound effect on the kinetics of the ATRP reaction.

the kinetics of surface-initiated ATOB polymerization of styrene from montmorillonite is dependent upon the surface-initiator density, with a seven-fold increase of the reaction rate observed at a graft density of 0.8 chains/nm2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of surface-initiated ATRA polymerization is a function of grafting density, and that this is a result of a shift in the equilibrium of the reaction in favor of the propagating species.
we have shown that the kinetics of surface-initiated ATRA can be dramatically affected by graft density and the resulting polymerization rate can vary by several orders of magnitude.
the grafting of initiator molecules on the surface of montmorillonite (clay) can be achieved through a simple reaction with the surface hydroxyl groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the graft density can be used as a kinetic control parameter in the surface-initiated polymerization of monomers from solid surfaces, and this can be exploited to tune the kinetics of polymerization reactions on surfaces.
surface-initiated polymerization reactions, such as ATRP, can be highly sensitive to the surface graft density.
the rate of surface-initiated ATRA polymerization can be enhanced by increasing the graft density.
